approved_translation: Cunning and deceit eventually trap the deceiver; beware of false promises in times of need.
translation_author: Ellen C. Babbitt (retold from traditional sources)
context_summary: In the Long Ago there was a summer when very little rain fell. All the Animals suffered for want of water, but the Fishes suffered most of all. But the Crab pinched the Crane's neck so that his head fell off. "Not my shell, but your bones are left to dry with the bones of the Fishes," said the Crab.
interpretation_boundaries: Do not depict specific historical Buddha figures — keep characters as generic animals or people
Focus on the moral lesson, avoid doctrinal Buddhist claims
